(ORAL)
RAVINDER DUDEJA, J.
1.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
This is a petition under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, seeking quashing of FIR No. 232/2024, dated 04.04.2024, registered at P.S Khajuri Khas, Delhi under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC and all proceedings emanating therefrom on the basis of settlement between the parties.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: The factual matrix giving rise to the instant case is that the marriage between Petitioner No. 1 and Respondent no. 2/complainant was solemnized on 19.02.2023 as per Muslim Rites and ceremonies.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: No child was born out of the said wedlock.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, on account of temperamental differences Petitioner No. 1 and Respondent No. 2 are living separately since 14.05.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. As per averments made in the FIR, Respondent No. 2 was subjected to physical and mental harassment on account of dowry demands by the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
FIR No. 232/2024 was lodged at the Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107636093/
1 instance of respondent no. 2 at PS Khajuri Khas under sections 498A/406/34 IPC against the petitioners.
4.

sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is submitted that petitioner no.1 and respondent no. 2 have obtained divorce on 29.07.2025 and the petitioner no. 1 has paid the entire settlement amount of Rs. 7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lacs only) and returned the jewellery articles to respondent no. 2 as per the schedule in the settlement.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Copy of the settlement agreement dated 16.07.2025 has been annexed as Annexure P-2.
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Petitioner nos. 1, 2, 3 and respondent no. 2 are physically present before the Court while petitioner nos. 4, 5, 6 & 7 have entered their appearance through VC.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: They have been identified by their respective counsels as well as by the Investigating Officer SI Sachin, from PS Khajuri Khas.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Respondent No. 2 confirms that the matter has been amicably settled with the petitioners without any force, fear, coercion and she has received the entire settlement and has no objection if the FIR No. 232/2024 is quashed against the Petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned Additional PP appearing for the State, also has no objection if the present FIR No. 232/2024 is quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Mohd. Sahil And Others vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 6 December, 2025.json

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable settlement of disputes in Rangappa Javoor vs The State Of Karnataka And Another, Diary No. 33313/2019, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 74,
Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr., (2013) 4 SCC 58 & in Gian Singh vs State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 9.
Further, it is settled that the inherent powers under section 482 of the Code are required to be exercised to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
Further, the High Court can quash non-compoundable offences after considering the nature of the offence and the amicable settlement between the concerned parties.
Supreme Court and this Court have repeatedly held that the cases arising out of matrimonial differences should be put to a quietus if the parties have reached an amicable settlement.
Reliance may be placed upon B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC.
10.
In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion, it would be in the interest of justice, to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
